ruling.recommended_action: Issue a $6.43 Ryde voucher to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment (extra_km × this trip's per-km rate); no account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip is a metered RydeTAXI job: the fare record shows distance $26.31 for 18.66 km and a total of $39.18, so detour kilometres enter the metered fare directly [F7][RD-2]. The GPS track records one off-route segment, 21:39–21:49, 6.27 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.71 km, adding 4.56 km and reaching up to 1958 m from the optimal route, against 18.7 km actual vs 13.9 km optimal overall [F3][F1][RD-1]. No percentage or kilometre threshold applies: any unexplained deviation breaches the driver's shortest-and-most-direct-route duty [RD-1].

No RD-4 excuse exists. The only traffic records are speed band 5 (40–49 km/h) on the Central Expressway and Kampong Bahru Road, there is no incident near the route during the trip window, and the weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4]. Band 5 is nowhere near the band 1/2 congestion RD-4(b) contemplates, and band evidence alone does not exempt in any event [RD-4].

On the consent question, the only rider message before the segment is Chat #2 at 21:36 — "Sure, no problem." — answering the driver's 21:35 request to "pull in at the petrol station just ahead for one minute? Tank is almost empty." [F8][F9]. The chat record is complete and every message is timestamped, so timing and completeness are settled [F10][RD-5]. What the rider agreed to is a one-minute stop of the driver's own (petrol for the car), not a route: the message names no road and no area, and the request is for the driver's errand, not for a way to VivoCity [F8][RD-5]. Neither advocate reads the exchange as a general route choice, so the general-route branch is not in play; the rider's reading is that the agreed scope does not cover the driven loop [F9][RD-5] and the driver's reading is that the agreed short stop was licence for "a small change of route" [F11]. A driver's post-trip statement that the rider agreed to a route is a claim, not rider consent, and cannot extend the rider's words [F11][RD-5]. The loop was a driver's own errand the rider did not ask for, so the segment counts and is refundable [F3][F8][F9][RD-5]. The rider-advocate's alternative branch is stronger still: the rider named no place at all, so the RD-3(a) exemption never attaches (no place named, and no stop at a petrol station appears anywhere in the segment) [F8][F3][RD-3]. The billed wait of 0.11 is a metered RydeTAXI waiting unit and stays chargeable [F5][RD-3(c)].

The refund is the segment's extra kilometres at this trip's per-kilometre rate, which the fare record itself states: distance fare $26.31 ÷ 18.66 km = $1.4100/km [F4][F7]. 4.56 km × $1.4100/km = $6.4300, i.e. $6.43 [F3][F4][RD-2]. The billed excess distance of $6.77 (4.80 km) exceeds the single segment's 4.56 km; the residual ~0.24 km is corridor/matching noise that RD-2 leaves with the driver, so only $6.43 is refundable — the figure both advocates converge on [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

No account flag: the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld in the prior 90 days (2 upheld overall, none route or no-show), so RD-6's "repeated breach" precondition is not met [F16][F17][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The only rider message before the 21:39 segment is Chat #2 21:36 'Sure, no problem.' in reply to the driver's 21:35 request to pull in at a petrol station 'for one minute' because his tank was almost empty — a stop for the driver's own errand, not a route [F8][F9]. It names no road or area, so it is neither a general route choice nor an agreed named road, and a driver's post-trip statement that a 'small change of route was fine' is a claim, not rider consent [F11][RD-5]. The 6.27 km driven where 1.71 km was optimal, adding 4.56 km, is therefore unexempted and refundable [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: D1 reads F9 'Sure, no problem.' as consent to 'a stop of that kind' before the segment [F8][F9], but the words fix a one-minute petrol stop for the driver's own car, and the recorded segment is a 6.27 km / 4.56 km-extra loop reaching 1958 m off the optimal route with no measured stop [F3]; the agreement therefore does not cover the driven segment [RD-5][RD-3].

D8 argues against an account flag; the flag is refused for a different reason than D8 gives — RD-6 needs a route dispute upheld in the prior 90 days, and F17 shows 0 route and 0 no-show upheld, so the precondition fails [F17][RD-6]. The refusal does not disturb the segment finding or the refund [F3][F4].

C9 asks for the RD-6 account flag; the profile shows 0 route disputes upheld in the prior 90 days (2 upheld overall, none route or no-show), so this case does not make the driver 'repeated' and no flag issues [F17][RD-6]. Profile facts cannot decide the deviation, which stands on F1 and F3 alone under RD-1.

what_would_change: F3: the judge found no rider agreement covering this segment, so $6.43 is refunded; a rider message agreeing to it before it started would have exempted it.
Had the driver carried a prior upheld route dispute in the last 90 days, RD-6 would add an account flag.
